items.title: One shared merge-lineage classifier (net endpoint diff, -z, maxBuffer, empty-diff means trusted, split catch) routes both the reuse and admissibility copies
items.context: Extract a shared helper (netDiffChangedPaths(evidenceHead,currentHead,gitCwd) + a shared lineage classifier) and route BOTH classifyTrustedValidationLineage (packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts:251) and validationHeadLineage (packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-admissibility.ts:42) through it. Net diff: git diff-tree -r --no-commit-id --name-only --no-renames -z <E> <C> with maxBuffer 1024*1024*1024; split on NUL. Empty net diff means trusted (remove the changed.length===0 -> rejected/empty-descendant-lineage/lineage_empty push). Split the try/catch so only merge-base --is-ancestor stays in the ancestry catch and a netDiffChangedPaths failure surfaces a distinct reason instead of mislabeling as not-ancestor. Keep the exact-head fast-path, the ancestor gate, and the isStoryMetadataPath untrusted filter unchanged; do not touch the other 8 reuse factors.

happy.desc: Import classifyMergeLineage from validation-lineage.ts in BOTH validation-evidence-reuse.ts (classifyTrustedValidationLineage) AND validation-evidence-admissibility.ts (validationHeadLineage) -> both call the same shared function; WHY: ensures one classifier routes both copies, no divergence possible

Run git diff-tree -r --no-commit-id --name-only --no-renames -z <evidenceHead> <currentHead> on a merge where only story-metadata paths changed -> net diff contains only metadata paths -> lineage classified as trusted; WHY: validates the core fix (net endpoint diff instead of per-commit -m union)
exact-head fast path preserved: evidenceHead === currentHead -> returns exact-head without spawning any git subprocess; WHY: regression guard on existing fast path

edge.desc: netDiffChangedPaths failure (e.g. invalid git ref) surfaces a DISTINCT reason string (not evidence-head-is-not-current-ancestor / lineage_not_ancestor) separate from the merge-base --is-ancestor catch -> caller can distinguish diff failure from ancestry failure; WHY: split-catch requirement

empty net diff between two distinct commits (evidenceHead != currentHead but tree-identical after merge) -> returns trusted (not rejected with empty-descendant-lineage/lineage_empty); WHY: verifies the length===0 rejection was removed
maxBuffer set to 1024*1024*1024 in the execFileSync call -> a diff producing >16MB of path output does not throw ENOBUFS; WHY: robustness for large repos

adversarial.desc: A mutation that restores the per-commit git diff-tree -m union (reverting to old algorithm) MUST cause the RED smoke assertion to fail, proving the fix is not bypassable by keeping old code; WHY: un-gameability requirement from story adversarial coverage

Both reuse and admissibility callers import from the SAME module path (validation-lineage.ts); grep for diff-tree.*-m in both consumer files returns zero matches -> the old per-commit approach cannot silently coexist; WHY: prevents divergence between copies

The other 8 reuse factors in evaluateRoutineValidationReuse remain unchanged: prior-command-execution-not-pass, material-hash-mismatch, story-files-hash-mismatch, identity-digest-mismatch, coverage-mismatch, dirty-tree, head-hash-missing, evidence-missing -> no collateral regression; WHY: scope containment

items.title: RED-first smoke reproduces the merge false-positive on both reuse and admissibility paths, with negative and robustness tests
items.context: New smoke (pattern per packages/main/src/tasks/evidence-refresh-smoke.ts: mkdtemp + git init + seed). (a) RED on unfixed code: merge a main branch lacking the story's committed source file, then assert classifyTrustedValidationLineage AND validationHeadLineage return rejected with untrusted-lineage-path/lineage_untrusted despite identical material/storyFiles/identity. (b) GREEN after fix: both return trusted; evaluateRoutineValidationReuse reusable=true and admissibility ok. (c) NEGATIVE (protection preserved): a genuine content change to a non-metadata file at the endpoint STILL refuses on both paths. (d) empty-net-diff between distinct heads means trusted; and a large-diff case exercising maxBuffer does not throw ENOBUFS. Wire the smoke into lattice.config.json validate.commands normal tier.

happy.desc: RED assertion: on a repo where main-merge re-lists the story source file via per-commit -m union, classifyTrustedValidationLineage returns rejected with untrusted-lineage-path AND validationHeadLineage returns rejected with lineage_untrusted, despite identical materialHash/storyFilesHash/identity.digest -> smoke FAILS on unfixed code; WHY: proves the bug is reproducible before fix

GREEN assertion: after applying the net endpoint diff fix, the same merge scenario causes BOTH classifyTrustedValidationLineage to return trusted-story-metadata-descendant AND validationHeadLineage to return trusted-story-metadata-descendant; evaluateRoutineValidationReuse reusable=true and admissibility ok=true; WHY: proves the fix resolves the false positive
Smoke is wired into lattice.config.json validate.commands normal tier and runs as part of npm test -> CI executes it; WHY: ensures ongoing regression protection

edge.desc: NEGATIVE test: a genuine content change to a non-metadata file at the endpoint STILL causes both classifyTrustedValidationLineage and validationHeadLineage to return rejected with the untrusted path listed -> protection preserved; WHY: the fix must not over-trust
empty-net-diff between two distinct heads (tree-identical merge) -> both paths return trusted (not rejected); WHY: edge case where merge commits exist but net content is unchanged
large-diff maxBuffer: a repo with >1000 changed paths in the net diff does not throw ENOBUFS or truncate the path list; WHY: robustness under realistic large-repo conditions

adversarial.desc: Mutation resistance: if the per-commit -m union is kept (reverting the fix in the shared classifier), the RED assertion MUST fire; the smoke structurally asserts the old algorithm fails -> a gameable fix that keeps -m is caught; WHY: un-gameability

Removing the NEGATIVE assertion (genuine content change still refuses) must be detectable as coverage loss: the smoke explicitly asserts untrusted paths are rejected, and removing that assertion causes the coverage report to flag missing required verification; WHY: prevents weakening the test

Both paths exercised in the SAME smoke: the smoke calls BOTH classifyTrustedValidationLineage AND validationHeadLineage (the admissibility copy) with the same git state and asserts matching results -> the two copies cannot silently diverge; WHY: shared-classifier convergence guarantee
